paras: The lynching of Frank Robertson took place at Bradley, in Lafayette County, Arkansas, near the Louisiana line, in late March 1903, when a party of about twenty-five men overpowered the jailer and carried off Robertson, a Black prisoner charged with arson. Robertson was reported lynched, although the first dispatches said his body had not been found and a Shreveport paper said it was found hanging from a tree. The case ran as a short wire item across the country and later appeared in lynching tallies kept by both white and Black papers.

Robertson was held in jail at Bradley on a charge of arson and, according to the dispatches, had confessed to setting fire to a store. A special to the Arkansas Gazette from New Lewisville added that there had been many cases of arson over the past year in the north Louisiana county adjoining Lafayette County.

The Caucasian of Shreveport said that a shotgun stolen from a store at Walnut Hill, Arkansas, burglarized and burned about three years earlier, had recently turned up with a man who said he had bought it. On that clue, it said, Roberson, as it spelled the name, was seized with a rope around his neck and confessed to that fire and other burnings.

According to the Gazette special, dated March 30, a party of twenty-five men "supposed to be from across the Louisiana line" rode into Bradley on the previous Thursday night, overpowered the jailer, took Robertson and rode away with him. An Associated Press dispatch from Lewisville gave the same account. The Pine Bluff Daily Graphic instead said he was lynched near Bradley "last Friday morning" by men said to have come from Louisiana.

The dispatches reported that the body had not been found, and a garbled printing of the Gazette special in the Caucasian said it was supposed to be in nearby canebrakes. The Caucasian's own account, which mentions neither the jail nor the riders, said he was hanged from a tree limb after confessing, and the body found there.

No lyncher was named, and no report of an inquest, arrests or grand jury action appears in the coverage. By midsummer Robertson's name was included in half-year lynching records, listed under March or under March 30 at Bradley, Arkansas.

White papers carried the story mainly in two nearly identical dispatches, the Associated Press text from Lewisville and the Gazette special relayed from Little Rock. It ran on March 31 in Savannah, Birmingham, Montgomery and Indianapolis papers, and over the next two weeks in Raleigh and in South Carolina weeklies. Headlines ran from "Negro Firebug Lynched" and "Negro Charged With Arson Put to Death" to "Mob Rode Up to the Jail and Took the Prisoner Away," and the Pickens People's Journal ran the Arkansas story as "Lynching in Louisiana." Northern weeklies cut it to a line or two.

Arkansas papers ran it as a state-news brief. The Caucasian of Shreveport was the only paper found to comment, calling Robertson "an old offender, a bold bad man" who had "set all law at defiance" and "a menace to any community," and it printed the story twice.

No Black-press news report or editorial on the case was found; the Black papers recorded it only in their lynching lists. The Seattle Republican listed him under the heading "Mobocracy's Bloody Reign," remarking that Russia and Turkey might emulate the record to do away with their Christians. The Sedalia Times listed "Frank Roberson, arson" in a "Record of Lynching" of men who had lost their lives "at the hands of a mob," while white papers such as the Hartford Herald printed similar lists without comment.

The date differs by source: the Gazette special placed the seizure on Thursday night, March 26, the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic on Friday morning, and the year-end lists on March 30, the date of the first Lewisville dispatch. The accounts also differ on how he died: the wire reports, which called their news meagre, described a raid on the jail and an unrecovered body, while the Caucasian described a rope confession and a hanging.

reader.title: Lynching of Frank Robertson
bases: A party of about twenty-five men took a jailed Black prisoner charged with arson from the jailer at Bradley and he was reported lynched (A5, A7); the Caucasian says he was hanged from a tree (A1).

Every report says Robertson was lynched, the wire adding that the body had not been found and the Caucasian that it was found hanging (A5, A7, A1); about twenty-five men overpowered the jailer to take him (A5), and the stated ground was his alleged arson and confession (A2, A1).

The AP and Arkansas Gazette dispatches (A7, A5), the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic (A6) and the Shreveport Caucasian's separate account (A1) all report that Robertson was lynched near Bradley after confessing to burning a store, though they differ on the date and on how he was taken and whether the body was found.

record_check.dossier: March 26 ('last Thursday night') per the Gazette special; the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic says Friday morning (March 27) and the year-end lists March 30.
The wire says he confessed to firing a store; only the Caucasian mentions burglary, and it says the confession was made with a rope around his neck.
Unnamed party of about twenty-five men supposed to be from across the Louisiana line.
True of the wire reports; the Caucasian says the body was found hanging from a tree.
Seizure from the jailer and killing; the Caucasian adds a rope-around-the-neck confession and hanging.
At least 21 white items in about 18 papers from March 29 to August 12, plus two Black-press lynching lists (Seattle Republican, Sedalia Times).
